explanation: For every i, use the count for i shifted right by one and add its low bit. This reuses the previously computed count for half of i.
timeComplexity: O(n) time for results from 0 through n. Each result after zero takes one previously computed count and one low-bit addition.
spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space excluding the O(n) output. The output array is the dynamic-programming table; loop indices need constant additional space.
attribution: Original repository-authored Blind75 C++ algorithm, promoted from the validated correct fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: The bits of i consist of the bits of i shifted right once, followed by its low bit. Therefore popcount(i)=popcount(i>>1)+(i&1). The shifted value is smaller, so its count is already available while filling the table in increasing order.
walkthrough: For n=6, begin with count[0]=0. Values 1..6 give 1,1,2,1,2,2 by reusing the count for their halves and adding their low bit. Return [0,1,1,2,1,2,2].
edgeCases: The output includes every value from zero through n.
The recurrence needs no binary-string conversion.
